checks.title: Same IRI used for two unrelated concepts
checks.description: One IRI is typed with two classes where neither is a specialisation of the other, so two mappings are minting the same identifier for different things.
checks.remediation: Decide which concept owns the IRI template and change the other mapping's BIND, or add the discriminator that keeps the two apart.
checks.cucumber_scenario: No IRI denotes two unrelated concepts

checks.title: Locally defined class has no place in the class hierarchy
checks.description: A class the model itself declares has no superclass and no subclass, so it sits outside the hierarchy: it inherits nothing, appears in no tree view, and no reasoner can relate its instances to anything else.
checks.remediation: Give it a superclass, or accept it as a top-level concept and say so by making something a subclass of it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every locally defined class has a place in the hierarchy

checks.title: Label or definition minted by the transformation
checks.description: A mapping states a skos:prefLabel, altLabel or definition for a term the model or taxonomy owns. Two files now disagree about the term's name the moment either changes, and the mapping's copy is the one that reaches the output.
checks.remediation: Delete the label from the mapping and let the taxonomy supply it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Vocabulary terms are named by the vocabulary

checks.title: Generated entity missing a required object property
checks.description: An entity of a class the project requires a link from does not have it. The rule is the project's, agreed in the mapping specification rather than declared in the ontology, which is why no registry check reports it.
checks.remediation: Fill the gap in the source, or change the mapping so an entity is not built at all when the link cannot be.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every generated entity carries the links its class requires

checks.title: Generated graph uses an unexpected modelling pattern
checks.description: A value is attached directly to an entity where the agreed pattern puts it on an intermediate node. The triple is valid and the number is right; what is lost is everywhere the unit and quantity kind would have gone.
checks.remediation: Build the intermediate node the pattern calls for, and move the value onto it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Values are attached the way the agreed pattern attaches them

checks.title: Magnitude missing a numeric value
checks.description: A magnitude node was built and typed but carries no number, usually because the source cell was empty and the mapping built the node anyway.
checks.remediation: Fill the source value, or make the mapping build the magnitude only when a value exists.

checks.title: Unit of measure incompatible with the quantity
checks.description: A magnitude carries a unit that does not measure its kind of quantity -- a pressure in litres, a length in seconds. The unit is a real unit and the link is the right link, so nothing structural can see it.
checks.remediation: Use a unit of the right kind, and check the mapping that chose it -- a wrong unit is usually a column read from the wrong place.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every magnitude is measured in a unit of its own kind

checks.title: Instance IRI built under a superseded base
checks.description: A BIND still CONCATs instance IRIs under the base agreed for a class that has since been replaced, typically because the concept moved into a shared namespace and took its agreed IRI pattern with it.
checks.remediation: Update the mapping's BIND to the pattern the superseding class declares, and decide what happens to the identifiers already issued.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Instance IRIs follow the pattern the current model agrees on

checks.metric: business key uniqueness within an output
checks.title: Two entities share a business key
checks.description: Two instances of one class carry the same value for the property the project treats as that class's business key, so one real-world thing has been created twice under two identifiers.
checks.remediation: Decide which identifier survives, merge the two, and give the source a uniqueness constraint on that key.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A business key identifies at most one entity

checks.title: Single-valued relationship carries two values
checks.description: An entity carries two values for a relationship the agreed pattern allows one of, typically because two mappings each contribute a link and disagree. Reported by a project check because the ontology does not declare the property functional.
checks.remediation: Establish which source is authoritative and drop the other mapping's triple. Declaring the property owl:FunctionalProperty afterwards moves the check to LOG-002.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A single-valued relationship has one value

checks.title: Template asserts a property outside its declared domain
checks.description: A CONSTRUCT template hangs a property off an entity whose class is not the property's rdfs:domain, nor a subclass of it. The suite reports the same condition as CNF-003, but of real output -- after the CSVs are read and the mappings run.
checks.remediation: Use the property the class actually has, or type the entity as the class the property expects. If both are right, the ontology's domain is too narrow.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every property a template asserts belongs to the class it is asserted on

checks.metric: deprecated term still built by a transformation
checks.title: Mapping still builds a deprecated term
checks.description: A mapping constructs a class or property the model marks owl:deprecated. QUA-003 asks this of an ontology and of data; neither reaches the mappings, which are where the use originates.
checks.remediation: Move the mapping to the replacement the ontology names, then decide what happens to the data already built with the old term.
checks.cucumber_scenario: No mapping builds a term the model has deprecated

checks.title: One prefix bound to two namespaces across the mapping set
checks.description: Two mappings bind the same prefix to different namespaces. Each file is internally consistent, so no per-file check fires; downstream the term-level checks report an undeclared term, which names the symptom in one file rather than the disagreement between two.
checks.remediation: Agree one namespace per prefix across the mapping set, preferably in a shared header the queries include rather than repeat.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A prefix means the same thing in every mapping
